seo.title: Google Business Profile Posts: Updates, Offers, Events
seo.meta_description: How Anaheim and Orange County businesses can use Google Business Profile posts: updates, offers and events, scheduling, rules and ideas that drive calls.

h1: Google Business Profile Posts: How to Use Updates, Offers and Events
answer: Google Business Profile posts let you share updates, offers and events directly on Search and Maps. Updates can include a photo or video and a button, offers need a title and dates, and events need a title and start and end dates. Posts older than 6 months are archived unless they have a date range. Anaheim and Orange County businesses can schedule posts and repeat them weekly or monthly.
key_takeaways: Posts archive after 6 months without a date range.
You can schedule and repeat posts.
Unverified phone numbers can get posts rejected.

sections.heading: What posts are for
sections.body_html: Google's help page says you can post updates on your Business Profile to share announcements, offers, updates and event details with customers on Search and Maps, and that seeing your latest updates helps customers decide to visit. For Orange County businesses, posts are a free way to show that the business is active, to promote seasonal offers and to answer common questions before customers call.

sections.heading: Where customers see posts
sections.body_html: On mobile, posts appear in the Updates or Overview tabs of the profile on Search and Maps. On a computer, they appear in the From the owner section. Google also describes featured posts on mobile, pulled from your profile posts or social channels such as Facebook and Instagram, currently available in English for single-location food and drink businesses in the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

sections.heading: Updates
sections.body_html: Updates share general information. You can add a description, a photo, a video and an action button with a link. Google says the button should take customers to a website where they can complete the action, such as booking, ordering online or learning more.

sections.heading: Offers
sections.body_html: Offers promote sales or deals. Google requires a title, dates and time, and adds a View offer button automatically. You can also include a description, photo, video, coupon code, link and terms and conditions.

sections.heading: Events
sections.body_html: Events promote something happening at your business. Add a title and start and end dates and times. Google notes that if you leave out start or end times, the event shows as lasting 24 hours on the event dates. You can add a description, photo, video and button.

sections.heading: How long posts last
sections.body_html: Google says posts older than 6 months are archived unless a date range is set. Offers and events use their dates; updates without dates fall off after six months, so refresh evergreen information periodically.

sections.heading: Scheduling and repeating posts
sections.body_html: When you create a post you can schedule it for a later date and time, and set it to repeat weekly, monthly or on a custom schedule. Multi-location businesses can share one post across several profiles. This makes it easy to plan a month of posts in one sitting.

sections.heading: Rules to follow
sections.body_html: Google reviews posts against its content policy. It warns that posts with a phone number in the description might be rejected if the number cannot be verified as connected to the business. Keep posts accurate, avoid misleading claims and use real photos.

sections.heading: Post ideas for local businesses
sections.body_html:
• Seasonal services, such as AC tune-ups before summer.
  • Holiday hours and special menus.
  • New services or products.
  • Recent projects with a photo.
  • Events, classes or open houses.
  • Answers to common questions, linking to a page on your site.

sections.heading: Posts and your website
sections.body_html: Link each post to a relevant page on your site rather than the homepage, using a button. A post about a new service should lead to that service's page, which helps customers act and keeps your profile and website telling the same story.

sections.heading: Post checklist
sections.body_html:
• Choose the right type: update, offer or event.
  • Offers have a title, dates and time.
  • Events have start and end dates and times.
  • A real photo or short video.
  • A button linking to the matching page on your site.
  • No unverified phone numbers in the description.
  • Scheduled ahead where possible.
  • Evergreen updates refreshed before 6 months.

sections.heading: A monthly post calendar
sections.body_html:
A simple rhythm keeps the profile current without much effort:

  • Week 1: an update about a service, linking to its page.
  • Week 2: a recent project or product with a photo.
  • Week 3: an offer with clear dates and terms, if you run one.
  • Week 4: an event, a seasonal tip or an answer to a common question.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine an HVAC company in Fullerton heading into summer. In May it schedules an update about AC tune-ups linking to its tune-up page, an offer for a seasonal inspection with clear start and end dates, and an update with a photo of a recent installation. It sets a monthly repeating post reminding customers to change filters. Customers who find the company on Maps see current, relevant information, and each post leads to the right page on the website.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Write one update linking to a service page.
  2. Schedule an offer or event with dates.
  3. Set one repeating monthly post.
  4. Check older updates before they archive.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Plenty of owners handle this themselves. Outside help pays off when time is short, when the business has many locations or when a problem is costing calls every day it stays unresolved. Be wary of anyone who promises guaranteed positions or asks for your verification codes or passwords; Google says nobody can pay for a better local ranking. Look for clear explanations, honest timelines and reporting tied to real enquiries. Chimera offers exactly that to businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Use updates for news, offers for deals and events for dates, schedule them ahead, link to the right page and refresh evergreen posts before they archive. Chimera, based in Anaheim, plans post calendars for Orange County businesses.

faqs.q: What are Google Business Profile posts?
faqs.a: Updates, offers and events you publish on your profile to share news, deals and dates on Search and Maps.

faqs.q: How long do Google posts last?
faqs.a: Google says posts older than 6 months are archived unless a date range is set.

faqs.q: Can I schedule Google Business Profile posts?
faqs.a: Yes, and you can set them to repeat weekly, monthly or on a custom schedule.
It may break Google's content policy; a phone number that cannot be verified as the business's can also cause rejection.

faqs.q: What does an offer post need?
faqs.a: A title, dates and time; Google adds a View offer button.
Google does not list posts as a ranking factor; they help customers decide and keep your profile current.
